# LeakSanitizer suppressions for php_excel CI.
#
# Format: "leak:<substring>" — substring must appear in any frame of
# the leak's stack trace.
#
# This file is intentionally empty at landing — php_excel's leak surface
# has not surfaced any process-lifetime allocations under the ASan
# CI job to date. Entries are added narrowly as known-good leaks are
# identified (e.g. vendored-library MINIT singletons). Prefer adding
# a narrow entry here over flipping ASAN_OPTIONS detect_leaks=0 in
# .github/workflows/tests.yml — see
# ~/ai/wiki/debugging/asan-php-extension.md for the recipe.
#
# To audit a new leak locally:
#   ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 LSAN_OPTIONS=fast_unwind_on_malloc=0 \
#     <asan-php> -d extension=php_excel.so -r '<repro>'

# libxl 5.2.0's xlTableRemoveFilter() leaks 72 bytes per call inside the SDK
# (operator new in libxl.so, not freed at xlBookRelease). Confirmed with a
# pure-C repro that never touches the extension, so it is a vendor bug, not an
# extension-side missing free — our ExcelTable::removeFilter() binding only
# calls the void libxl function and has no handle to release. libxl is shipped
# stripped (frames are bare libxl.so+offset with no symbol), so the narrowest
# practical match is the library name. Reported to libxl support; remove this
# entry once a fixed SDK ships. Tradeoff: this also masks a hypothetical
# forgotten xlBookRelease (whose allocation frames are also inside libxl.so) —
# book release is structural (object free handler) and covered by the
# stale-wrapper tests, so the risk is low.
leak:libxl.so
